title: M74 — The Phantom Galaxy
subtitle: Spiral galaxy in Pisces, 30 million light-years away
alt: An infrared view of the spiral galaxy M74: a brilliant white core, spiral arms traced in magenta and pink dust, and scattered blue stars against black space.
facts: Astronomers using NASA's Spitzer Space Telescope spotted a dust factory 30 million light-years away in the spiral galaxy M74. The factory sits at the scene of a massive star's explosive death, or supernova.

hotspots.name: The galactic core
hotspots.text: The centre of M74. It is the brightest thing in this frame, and it is 30 million light-years away.

hotspots.name: The upper arm
hotspots.text: A spiral arm, lit up in pink. This is an infrared picture, so what glows here is warm dust, not starlight.

hotspots.name: The lower arm
hotspots.text: The other side of the spiral. Follow it outwards and the dust thins into black space.

hotspots.name: The dust factory
hotspots.text: Somewhere in this galaxy, Spitzer found a dust factory: the wreckage of a massive star that exploded.
